bug_semantics: AzureKeyVaultBackend, in multi-team mode, looks up a Connection or Variable by first probing the caller's team-scoped vault name and, on miss, falling through to a team-agnostic lookup that uses the caller-supplied id as the secret name. A guard `_is_team_specific_accessed_as_global` was meant to stop an id that already names a team namespace, but it is gated on `team_name is None`, so it never runs for a team-scoped caller. A caller authorized for team A can therefore pass an id that spells out another team's namespace (after the TEAM_SEP refactor, e.g. `otherteam--secret`); the team-A probe misses and the fall-through returns that other team's credentials in full (CWE-639).
flaw_origin: The miss-then-global fall-through and the `team_name is None` guard were first written in reconstructable PR #65692 member 933d5676f96dba4d202c1e5938ca42f564fe01f1 while adding multi-team lookup to AzureKeyVaultBackend. The parent `_get_secret` was a single unscoped vault get that ignored `team_name`. Later members of the same PR introduced TEAM_SEP `--` and retargeted the guard regex but left the fall-through and the `team_name is None` gate intact; GitHub squash 462b8e159614e3eba71febfc2a70fcbf665cbb47 landed that snapshot on main.
